- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust downward by 1–3% to avoid missing downside.
- Model often overshoots after recent spikes (especially >68.0); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast peak if prior 3–5 days show high sentiment or price surge.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 65–68 range, model tends to overreact; dampen forecast by 1–4% in next 3–5 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model consistently overestimates later days (especially 20–30) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative — reduce final 5–10 days by 1–3%.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model may misread momentum; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment “reset” or “reversal” phase.
